title: Choose the session screen's layout
question: Three ways to arrange a live session. Each shows the same moment: Ada asks Josephine to run 1010 through her DFA. Lock one, steer it, or re-roll.

options.label: Living notebook
options.thesis: The session is a notebook of moments; the live one owns the full width at the bottom.
options.viewport: Earlier hints and snapshots stack above; the live paper feed with Ada's markup fills the bottom card, captions beneath, Ada and the controls on a right rail.
options.risk: Reads like a chat app, which Tassel says it isn't, and paper and board can only stack, never sit side by side.

options.label: One stage, her work first
options.thesis: Her paper owns the window, and the board slides in beside it when Ada has something to show.
options.viewport: Paper left and board right at 50/50 for the counterexample, Ada's tile floating top-right, captions as subtitles, a pill dock at the bottom.
options.risk: Ada is small on screen, so she can read as a sticker rather than a person.

options.label: A call with your tutor
options.thesis: A familiar call layout: Ada is on the call, and whatever she shows takes the main tile.
options.viewport: Ada's board and markup fill the main tile, a right filmstrip holds Ada (large) and Josephine's paper, and a call bar runs along the bottom.
options.risk: Spends prime space on the avatar and feels like a meeting app rather than a desk.
